title: Canonical tensor constraints and associativity for one projection mate
statement:
Canonical tensor constraints and associativity for one projection mate. In the existing RingedTensorCorner, RingedTensorModel and RingedTensorEdge interfaces, with TensorConstraints and the normalized comparison predicates of lem-sfb-ringed-projection-tensor-composition, assert exactly the following independent part of its coherence calculation:

theorem ringedProjectionTensorAssociativity
    {X Y : RingedTensorCorner.{u, w}} (f : RingedTensorEdge Y X)
    (a : RingedTensorModel X) (b : RingedTensorModel Y) :
    ∃ (tx : TensorConstraints X a) (ty : TensorConstraints Y b),
      (∀ (E : X.mateDerived) (Q T : Y.mateDerived),
        f.projection b a E (Y.tensor.obj (Q, T)) ≫
            f.right.map (X.tensor.map
              (Prod.mkHom (𝟙 E) ((f.tensorComparison b a).hom.app (Q, T)))) ≫
            f.right.map (tx.associator E (f.left.obj Q) (f.left.obj T)).inv =
          (ty.associator (f.right.obj E) Q T).inv ≫
            Y.tensor.map (Prod.mkHom (f.projection b a E Q) (𝟙 T)) ≫
            f.projection b a (X.tensor.obj (E, f.left.obj Q)) T)

source.place: Tags 0B56 (equation-projection-formula-map), 0DV0 (categories.tex, lemma-compose-counits); formal tensor-associativity and section specialization of the canonical projection mate

proof.text: Choose the canonical constraints from ringedProjectionTensorStructure. Transpose the two paths through the given adjunction. The two counit equations and tensorator naturality reduce the right path to the tensor of the counit and two identities. Use associator naturality to move the counit, then the structural associativity equation identifies the paths. Injectivity of the Hom equivalence completes the argument.
